commenti.body: Does anyone know if you can get *The Man Who Stole the Sun* on Region 1 or region-free DVD or Blu-ray? I've been looking, but I can't find it anywhere.

After re-watching Akira for the nth time and still having my mind blown by the audio-visual experience, yet again I sat there like an absent minded toddler when thinking about the narrative. As one does on the internet, I ventured to explore if I was alone in this experience and to my joy... I was not. Curious at the heated discussions on the topic I decided to have a look see through the manga, the creator's insights, and other sources on 'Why Akira Doesn't Make Sense'. Here's my take in the form of a video essay, give it a watch, let me know what you think. Any and all feedback is appreciated :)

[https://youtu.be/WBNaGA1dZig](https://youtu.be/wbnaga1dzig)
Any thoughts on the film of Mary Pickford?

That's a pretty damn broad question, because just about every movie can be viewed as a study of humanity to some degree. So as I'm not exactly sure what you're looking for, I just list a few of my favourites which relate to the subject matter in some way or other:

The Act of Killing & The Look of Silence  
Killers of the Flower Moon  
Apocalypse Now  
Roma  
Nashville  
City of God  
High and Low  
I Compagni  
Lazzaro Felice  
Do the Right Thing  
Amarcord  
Aguirre, the Wrath of God  
...

I am looking for the name of a french film I watched as teenager probably over 10 years ago. Maybe someone here can help me find out the name. I have vague memories about it.  
I remember a man, an engineer I think. Interested in mathematics, admirer of the mathematician and philosopher Blaise Pascal. A Devout Christian meeting an atheistic woman through a friend.  
The film is about their relationship.  
It has scenes on the beach. Probably French New Wave. Black and White.

Watched *American Fiction* the other night and the shallowest thought I have about the film is that  Jeffrey Wright is just delightful as a snobby author/lit professor. The palpable disgust and judgement on his face when he disapproves of something was so amusing. Brings me back to seeing that facial expression on some of my lit professors at uni. I'd be happy if he won the Oscar.
Where do I find more great films like Taxi Driver (1976)? I recently started watching old movies and I want to find more great films. I like action, scifi. Can someone give me some recommendation?

When I started out watching movies more "seriously", I just went through all of the movies in the IMDb Top 250 (which at the time was very good, but not anymore). A more popular choice today would be the [Letterboxd 250](https://letterboxd.com/dave/list/official-top-250-narrative-feature-films/) (which is fine, but somehow doesn't even include Taxi Driver) and my personal favourite is the 2012 Sight & Sound directors' poll. Roger Ebert's list of [great movies](https://www.rogerebert.com/great-movies) is also a great source of inspiration, especially in combination with his beautifully written reviews.
Check out After Hours, it’s not exactly action or scifi but it’s my favourite Scorsese and a fantastic, if a bit absurd, thriller.
